paper.title_en: BAO and Type Ia Supernovae in LTB Cosmology: Constraints on Radial Inhomogeneity and Acoustic-Ruler Evolution
paper.abstract_en: We investigate how baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) and Type Ia supernovae constrain radial density profiles and acoustic-ruler evolution in Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi (LTB) cosmology with a cosmological constant. A consistent extension of a homogeneous analysis requires modified distances and unequal radial and transverse ruler stretching. Transverse BAO and supernovae isolate ruler evolution without fixing its absolute length. We connect this test to exact nonlinear, compensated density profiles with free depth, width, shell location and exterior matter density, keeping the observer at the symmetry centre. We fit DESI DR2 BAO and DES-Dovekie supernovae with full covariances and matched calibration freedom in LTB and flat $Λ$CDM. Conditional on evaluating BAO predictions at effective redshifts, LTB improves the full-sample $χ^2$ by 8.5 with three additional parameters. DESI rejects the specific deep profile preferred without it, while distinct profiles remain nearly degenerate. Selecting DES supernovae alone gives a shallower shell and a gain of 7.44, almost entirely from BAO and unchanged by an additional magnitude-uncertainty cut. Two illustrative redshift-window tests retain a DES-only gain close to 7 at this geometry. The preferred profile and ruler history depend on the supernova selection. The full-sample gain occurs in at least 7% of simulated flat-$Λ$CDM data sets and does not establish an inhomogeneity detection; this calibration is not transferred to DES-only fits. Small finite-ruler corrections do not validate survey-bin averaging. In the local approximation, common LTB ruler evolution shifts angular and transverse three-dimensional BAO together and cannot by itself explain their discrepancy.
